sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section details the patient's demographic profile, medical history, and the chronological evolution of symptoms from the initial adverse reaction to semaglutide to the onset of progressive neuromuscular decline. It focuses on distinguishing the initial acute toxicity (GI symptoms, dehydration, acute kidney injury) from the subsequent subacute development of immune-mediated pathology.
subtopics: Patient demographics and relevant medical history (Obesity, NAFLD, Hypertension)
Temporal relationship: Single-dose exposure to semaglutide and immediate GI/toxic reactions
Evolution of symptoms: From deconditioning to progressive proximal weakness, dysphagia, and dysphonia
Differentiating early rhabdomyolysis markers vs. delayed myopathic progression
Initial exclusion of common causes: Statin history, trauma, infection, and metabolic derangements

sections.description: This section provides the necessary theoretical background to understand Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM), contrasting it with toxic myopathies and classic inflammatory myopathies. It establishes the diagnostic criteria used to rule out alternative etiologies in this specific case.
subtopics: Overview of IMNM: Pathophysiology of necrosis with paucity of lymphocytes
Comparison: Drug-induced toxic rhabdomyolysis vs. Autoimmune IMNM kinetics
Role of autoantibodies: Significance of Anti-HMGCR/SRP positivity vs. Seronegative IMNM
Evaluating confounding factors: Hepatic transaminitis (AST/ALT) source differentiation (liver vs. muscle)
Cardiac involvement assessment: Ruling out myocarditis vs. stress cardiomyopathy in myopathy contexts

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Multimodal Evidence Synthesis
sections.description: A comprehensive review of the investigative steps taken to confirm the diagnosis. This section analyzes laboratory trends, advanced imaging findings (MRI), serological profiles, and crucial histological evidence from muscle biopsy that solidified the diagnosis of IMNM.
subtopics: Laboratory interpretation: CK trajectory (12-fold rise), inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP), and seronegative status
Imaging analysis: MRI findings of symmetric proximal muscular edema and cardiac MRI results
Histopathological gold standard: Muscle biopsy findings (necrosis, regeneration, macrophage infiltration/myophagocytosis)
Immunohistochemistry insights: MAC deposition patterns and CD68/CD3 cell distribution
Exclusionary testing results: Negative myositis panel ruling out overlap syndromes
